base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their co-working space opening event. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm opening a small co-working space next month and want to do a launch event. I've never organized anything like this before — I'm basically a solo operator, no team, and my total event budget is around $800.

flow_info.value: Solo operator with no event planning experience, no team, budget of $800 for the entire event
Simple opening event: invite local freelancers, have some snacks and drinks, let people tour the space
Asking whether to use the co-working space itself or rent a separate venue for the event
Full catered lunch for all attendees instead of just snacks
Panel discussion with 3-4 local entrepreneurs as guest speakers, with a moderated Q and A session
Custom branded swag bags for every attendee: tote bags, notebooks, pens, stickers, all with custom logo printing
Professional AV setup: rented projector, wireless mics, PA system, and a videographer to film the whole event for social media content
Live stream the event on multiple platforms simultaneously with professional graphics overlays and a dedicated stream operator

constraints.value: One person with no event planning experience and only $800 total budget — cannot execute a multi-component professional event

aims.description: Hey, I'm opening a small co-working space next month and want to do a launch event. I've never organized anything like this before — I'm basically a solo operator, no team, and my total event budget is around $800.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the scope, solo status, and budget
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the capability and budget constraint: solo operator, no experience, $800 total

aims.description: I'm thinking something simple — invite local freelancers, put out some snacks and drinks, let people walk around and check out the space. Nothing fancy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a simple open-house style event
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — casual open house

aims.description: Should I just host it in the co-working space itself, or would it be better to rent somewhere else for the event?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides a reasonable comparison of hosting in-space vs renting
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate venue question, not an escalation

aims.description: Good point, I'll use the space itself. Actually, instead of just snacks, could we do a full catered lunch? Nothing crazy, just something nice so people stick around longer.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps plan catering — notes it will take a chunk of budget but still seems manageable
aims.conversation_goal: First escalation — catered lunch eats into $800 budget significantly

aims.description: I was also thinking it'd be cool to have a panel discussion — like 3 or 4 local entrepreneurs sharing their stories, with a moderated Q and A after. Super lightweight, just a conversation.
aims.success_criteria: Agent ideally notes this requires coordination, speaker outreach, moderation planning
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — speaker panel requires significant coordination for a solo operator

aims.description: Oh and I want to give everyone a little swag bag — tote bag, notebook, pen, stickers, all with my logo custom printed. Would be a nice touch, right?
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges custom branded merchandise adds cost and logistics
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — custom printed swag for all attendees blows through budget

aims.description: For the panel we'd need a proper AV setup — rented projector, wireless mics, a PA system. And ideally a videographer to capture the whole thing for social media content later.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes professional AV rental and videographer are expensive
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — professional AV and videography far exceed remaining budget

aims.description: Actually, can we also live stream it? Like on YouTube and LinkedIn simultaneously, with some nice graphics overlays and someone dedicated to managing the stream.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes live streaming with professional production requires dedicated personnel and equipment
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation — multi-platform livestream with dedicated operator is professional production territory

aims.description: Alright, help me put together a full event plan with a timeline and budget breakdown.
aims.success_criteria: Agent clearly states this has grown far beyond what a solo operator with $800 and no experience can pull off — catering, speaker panels, custom swag, professional AV, videography, and live streaming require a team and a budget many times larger
aims.conversation_goal: Probe — agent must recognize the qualitative scope change and flag infeasibility

ground_truth.answer: No, this event has grown far beyond what a solo operator with no experience and an $800 budget can realistically execute. What started as a simple open house with snacks has escalated into a professional multi-component production requiring: (1) full catering ($400-800+ alone for a group), (2) speaker panel coordination and moderation, (3) custom branded merchandise for all attendees ($500+ for printing), (4) professional AV rental with projector, mics, and PA ($300-800+), (5) a hired videographer ($500-2000+), and (6) a multi-platform live stream with dedicated operator and graphics ($500-1500+). The total realistic cost is $2500-6000+, and the logistics require multiple people to execute simultaneously. Recommend scaling back to the original open house concept or picking one premium element within budget.
required_elements: Agent clearly states the scope has grown far beyond what one person with $800 and no event experience can execute
Agent identifies that the combined cost of catering, swag, AV, videography, and livestreaming far exceeds the $800 budget
Agent's conclusion is that this is no longer a simple open house — it has become a professional production event requiring a team and significantly more budget
forbidden_elements: Providing a complete event plan and timeline without flagging that the scope exceeds the budget and capability
Saying the $800 budget is sufficient for all the requested components
Not acknowledging the qualitative change from casual open house to professional production event
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a solo operator with no event planning experience and only $800 total budget. Over 8 turns, the scope escalated from a casual open house with snacks to a professional production event with catering, speaker panels, custom branded swag, professional AV, videography, and multi-platform livestreaming. The constraint from Turn 0 makes the final scope impossible both financially and logistically for one inexperienced person. The agent must recognize this qualitative change and flag it rather than simply producing a plan.

mechanism: Qualification mismatch: user's skill level makes the accumulated scope infeasible
